lithos_version: lithos 0.5.0 @ a4d2d62 (source read 2026-10-04); every envelope below is the source's, and each was also probed against a newer live Lithos (MCP serverInfo 3.2.0) — differences are recorded in observed_divergences, never substituted

request.notes: The whole request surface: a terminal (completed/cancelled) task back to `open`. Clears `resolved_at` and `outcome`, records the reopen as a finding reading `[Reopened] task reopened (was <prior status>)`, plus `; prior outcome: <outcome>` when there was one (the only surviving evidence of it — see tasks.REOPENED_FINDING_PREFIX) and emits `task.reopened`. An already-open task is `task_not_resolved`, a missing one `task_not_found`. Every id goes through the SHARED resolver (`resolve_task_id`): a value of 36 or more characters is a full id and passes through untouched, a miss included, to this tool's own lookup; anything shorter than `MIN_PREFIX_LEN` (6) is `invalid_input`; anything between is searched as a PREFIX — matching nothing is the resolver's own `task_not_found` ("No task matches id prefix …", a different message from this tool's own not-found, same code) and matching several is `ambiguous_id_prefix` (`AmbiguousIdPrefixError`, mapped by `tool_span`) with up to `AMBIGUITY_CANDIDATE_CAP` (5) `{id, title}` candidate RECORDS, the message stating the capped count. Every envelope is `{status, code, message}` plus, for that one code, `candidates` — the coordination errors here carry no other key. Lens sends a full id for this tool (the funnel acts on a task it has just read), so none of the prefix refusals is on a Lens request; all are vendored because the mapper must still answer them.

errors.message: Task 'influx-gate-human' is already open; nothing to reopen.
task_id 'infl' is too short: pass the full task id or a prefix of at least 6 characters.
Task id prefix '506155' (task_id) is ambiguous: 2 or more matches. Retry with a longer prefix or a full id from candidates.

observed_divergences: None in shape. The success payload is the tool's return dict verbatim (`{success, reblocked, task_id, title, updated_at}`); `reblocked` is a list of task IDS, not records. `newly_reblocked_by` returns [] unless the task was COMPLETED — reopening a CANCELLED task un-strands its dependents (they were `blocker_unsatisfiable`, not ready) and re-blocks nobody, the `cancelled_reopen` variant — and otherwise each OPEN `blocks` / `waits_on_gate` dependent whose current blockers are this task alone. That is why T3 D8 counts the cancelled case from the task's own active outgoing dependency edges instead. Both refusals are `reopen_task`'s own: "Task '…' not found." for a full-length id with no row, and "Task '…' is already open; nothing to reopen." — an earlier pass of this slice had composed the latter as "… is not resolved (status: open).", which the source never says. The success payload itself is not probed live: it would reopen a real task. Live check: the envelopes and order above were also probed (2026-10-04) against the Lithos this environment reaches, serverInfo 3.2.0 — NEWER than a4d2d62 (it serves `lithos_task_edge_delete`, added after 0.5.0) — with requests the server refuses, so nothing was written.
